domains.title: Snowflake AI Data Cloud Features and Architecture
domains.description: Understand Snowflake platform capabilities, architecture, interfaces, editions, storage primitives, and AI/application-development features.

skills.title: Outline key Snowflake AI Data Cloud features
skills.objective: Recognize the platform capabilities and design principles that distinguish Snowflake across data, applications, AI, collaboration, and governance.
exam_traps: Treating Snowflake as only a traditional data warehouse.
Assuming every workload requires a user-managed warehouse.

skills.title: Outline Snowflake architecture
skills.objective: Explain the storage, compute, and cloud services layers and how their separation affects concurrency, scaling, management, and cost.
exam_traps: Confusing virtual warehouses with persistent data storage.
Assuming separate warehouses create separate copies of data.

skills.title: Outline Snowflake interfaces and client tools
skills.objective: Choose among Snowsight, Snowflake CLI, SnowSQL, drivers, connectors, APIs, and developer tooling for a given access pattern.
exam_traps: Confusing a driver with a data-ingestion connector.
Treating SnowSQL and Snowflake CLI as identical tooling.

skills.title: Outline Snowflake editions
skills.objective: Differentiate Standard, Enterprise, Business Critical, and Virtual Private Snowflake by feature availability and workload requirements.
exam_traps: Choosing an edition only by warehouse size.
Assuming every security feature exists in Standard Edition.

skills.title: Explain Snowflake storage concepts and object types
skills.objective: Understand micro-partitions, pruning, clustering, table types, Iceberg tables, dynamic tables, hybrid tables, external tables, and view types.
exam_traps: Treating micro-partitions as user-managed partitions.
Confusing dynamic tables with streams or materialized views.

skills.title: Explain AI/ML and application-development features
skills.objective: Recognize Snowflake Notebooks, Streamlit in Snowflake, Snowpark, Cortex AI functions, Cortex Search, Cortex Analyst, Document AI, and Snowflake ML use cases.
exam_traps: Using Cortex Search when the requirement is natural-language SQL over structured semantic models.
Confusing Snowpark with a client-side pandas-only library.

domains.title: Account Management and Data Governance
domains.description: Secure identities and networks, govern sensitive data, monitor account usage, and control Snowflake spend.

skills.title: Explain Snowflake security model and access principles
skills.objective: Apply RBAC, MFA, SSO, OAuth, key-pair authentication, authentication/network policies, and security posture controls such as Trust Center.
exam_traps: Granting routine access directly to users instead of roles.
Using a network policy as a substitute for authentication controls.

skills.title: Define and apply Snowflake data governance
skills.objective: Use masking policies, row access policies, tags, classification, lineage, and governance controls to protect and understand data.
exam_traps: Confusing column masking with row filtering.
Assuming tags enforce protection without a policy or process that consumes them.

skills.title: Explain monitoring and cost management
skills.objective: Use resource monitors, budgets, ACCOUNT_USAGE, organization/account usage views, warehouse metering, and cost-attribution concepts.
exam_traps: Assuming resource monitors optimize SQL.
Ignoring serverless-feature consumption when analyzing total cost.

domains.title: Data Loading, Unloading, and Connectivity
domains.description: Move data into and out of Snowflake, automate ingestion, and connect Snowflake securely to external systems.

skills.title: Perform data loading and unloading
skills.objective: Use stages, file formats, COPY INTO, load validation, error handling, directory tables, and unload patterns for file-based data movement.
exam_traps: Confusing COPY INTO <table> with COPY INTO <location>.
Treating a file format as the storage location itself.

skills.title: Perform automated data ingestion
skills.objective: Choose Snowpipe, Snowpipe Streaming, streams, tasks, and dynamic tables appropriately for continuous ingestion and incremental processing.
exam_traps: Assuming Snowpipe Streaming reads staged files.
Confusing stream change tracking with task scheduling or dynamic-table refresh.

skills.title: Identify Snowflake connectors and integrations
skills.objective: Recognize drivers, Kafka/Spark connectors, storage integrations, API integrations, external access integrations, and related connectivity boundaries.
exam_traps: Putting long-lived cloud credentials in SQL when an integration should be used.
Confusing client connectivity with bulk/streaming ingestion.

domains.title: Performance Optimization, Querying, and Transformation
domains.description: Diagnose query behavior, size and scale compute, use Snowflake SQL features, and work with semi-structured and unstructured data.

skills.title: Explain query performance concepts
skills.objective: Distinguish caching layers, micro-partition pruning, clustering, Query Profile signals, search optimization, and Query Acceleration Service.
exam_traps: Treating every performance problem as a warehouse-sizing problem.
Confusing persisted result reuse with warehouse-local cache.

skills.title: Use warehouse sizing and scaling
skills.objective: Choose scale-up versus scale-out, configure auto-suspend/resume, use multi-cluster warehouses, and balance latency, concurrency, and credit consumption.
exam_traps: Using multi-cluster to speed up one CPU-bound query.
Assuming a larger warehouse always costs more overall or always costs less overall.

skills.title: Use Snowflake query and transformation features
skills.objective: Apply QUALIFY, window functions, PIVOT/UNPIVOT, MERGE, UDFs, stored procedures, tasks, Snowpark, and SQL transformation patterns.
exam_traps: Using HAVING when the requirement is to filter on a window-function result.
Confusing a UDF with a stored procedure.

skills.title: Use semi-structured and unstructured data
skills.objective: Work with VARIANT, OBJECT, ARRAY, JSON pathing, FLATTEN, staged unstructured files, directory tables, file URLs, and Document AI.
exam_traps: Forgetting that FLATTEN is a table function commonly used laterally.
Treating unstructured file metadata as if it were the file contents.

domains.title: Data Collaboration
domains.description: Recover and protect data, share live data securely, clone environments efficiently, and replicate Snowflake objects for resilience and collaboration.

skills.title: Explain Time Travel and Fail-safe
skills.objective: Use AT/BEFORE and UNDROP during the retention window, understand retention differences, and distinguish user-accessible Time Travel from Snowflake-managed Fail-safe.
exam_traps: Treating Fail-safe as a queryable historical-data feature.
Assuming transient and temporary objects have the same recovery guarantees as permanent objects.

skills.title: Explain secure data sharing and collaboration
skills.objective: Understand direct shares, listings, reader accounts, Marketplace, Native Apps, and Data Clean Rooms as collaboration patterns without unnecessary data copies.
exam_traps: Assuming secure sharing copies provider data into the consumer account.
Using a reader account for a consumer that already has its own Snowflake account without a specific reason.

skills.title: Explain zero-copy cloning and replication
skills.objective: Use zero-copy cloning for fast writable copies and distinguish it from replication/failover used to copy supported objects across accounts or regions.
exam_traps: Confusing cloning with cross-region disaster recovery.
Assuming cloned objects never incur additional storage as they diverge.
